Here is how to tell the difference before you add one to your site. Modern AI chatbots can hold a natural conversation, which makes them tempting for any business that gets a steady stream of questions. Done well, a chatbot answers instantly, captures leads after hours and frees your staff for work that needs a person. Done badly, it gives confident wrong answers and drives customers away. Captures inquiries after hours by collecting a name, contact details and a short description, then passing them to you. Points people to the right page, such as your booking form, menu, price list or contact page. Speaks several languages, which helps if your customers do not all prefer English. What It Should Not Do Invent prices, availability or promises. If the answer is not in the information you gave it, it should say so and offer to connect the visitor with a person. Give medical, legal or financial advice. Clinics, law offices and accountants need especially careful limits. Hide the human option. Every chat should make it easy to call, email or request a callback. Collect more personal data than it needs. Ask only for what you will actually use, and say how it will be handled. There is no "mixed content," meaning images or scripts still loading over plain HTTP. Modern browsers label non-HTTPS pages as "Not secure," so this layer protects your reputation as much as your data.
